clue.text: Fish bar for the birds

a rod on which a bird rests

explanation.surface: A fish-and-chip bar that caters for birds.

clue.text: One hampered by a desire to eat out?

explanation.surface: Someone held back by wanting to go to a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes a meal outdoors, often carrying a basket of food.

clue.text: Brief military survey sounds destructive!

parts.note: wrecky, as slangily said, means given to wrecking

explanation.definitionFit: Short for reconnaissance, an exploratory military survey.

clue.text: Principal is not short of part of a bridle

tall is the opposite of short

explanation.definitionFit: The strap of a bridle or halter that goes round the horse's head.

clue.text: Continuity shooting on set, in a word

parts.words: Continuity shooting on set, in a word
parts.note: film-set words (continuity, shooting) hide a description of a continuous volley of gunfire, summed up in a single word

clue.text: "Taffeta phrases, silken terms precise … — pedantical" (L. L. Lost)

definitions.text: "Taffeta phrases, silken terms precise … — pedantical" (L. L. Lost)

parts.words: "Taffeta phrases, silken terms precise … — pedantical" (L. L. Lost)
parts.note: a quotation from Love's Labour's Lost with the missing word to be supplied before pedantical

explanation.surface: A line from Berowne's speech renouncing fancy language in Love's Labour's Lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The full lines run: 'Taffeta phrases, silken terms precise, Three-piled hyperboles, spruce affectation, ___ pedantical'.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures of speech, rhetorical devices that Berowne calls pedantic.

clue.text: Group that's in risky ventures

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for ventures

parts.note: specs are speculations, risky investments
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A group of people involved in risky enterprises.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological category grouping similar organisms that can interbreed.

clue.text: Plants sprung from 12, would you say ?

indicators.note: a question about speech, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: 12 across is a downpour, from which leaks spring in a roof

explanation.surface: Asking whether plants grew out of a rainstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetables of the onion family, emblem of Wales.

clue.text: A manhole's shifted to reach the museum

indicators.note: shifted means moved about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive gives its S here as a letter of the pool

explanation.surface: Moving a manhole cover to get to the museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashmolean is Oxford University's museum of art and archaeology.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's famous museum, founded on Elias Ashmole's collection.

clue.text: Where Derby records are on order

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Where the results of the Derby horse race are kept in sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's great flat horse race, run on the Surrey downs at this town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey racecourse town that hosts the Derby each summer.

clue.text: Elgar's London, a local anaesthetic you say?

explanation.surface: A query about whether Elgar's London is some local numbing drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's concert overture 'Cockaigne (In London Town)' takes its title from the old mock name for London.
explanation.definitionFit: The fanciful land of plenty became a jocular name for London, and Elgar's overture of that title portrays the city.

clue.text: Point to one who doubted the national character

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
Thos is short for Thomas, the doubting apostle

explanation.surface: Pointing to a doubter as typical of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The guiding spirit or characteristic outlook of a people or community.

clue.text: The Times represented bits of news

indicators.note: re-presented, that is set out again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The newspaper reproduced snippets of news.
explanation.definitionFit: Short reports in a newspaper are called pieces or articles.

clue.text: Drop-scene by artist in The Tempest?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
a tempest is a storm

explanation.surface: A theatre drop-cloth painted by an artist for a production of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop-scene' looks like theatre scenery but means a scene of falling drops.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is literally a scene of drops of water falling.

clue.text: Old carriers had their troubles in the Great War

clue.text: On which lack of equilibrium makes the trip go wrong

clue.text: Distinguished family also of good standing

explanation.surface: A well-known family that is also highly respected.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell were the famous literary siblings; the name reads as 'sit well', a jokey twist on 'good standing'.

clue.text: Aromatic herb used with a Spanish port wine

parts.note: tarragon is an aromatic herb

clue.text: Underdogs deter us from going a-hunting

the fairies of William Allingham's poem: 'We daren't go a-hunting for fear of ...'

explanation.walkthrough: Allingham's 'The Fairies' begins 'Up the airy mountain, Down the rushy glen, We daren't go a-hunting For fear of little men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary people with no power, and the fairy folk feared in Allingham's poem.

clue.text: Film butler once helped to fill the gap

clue.text: After second drink painting looks dotty

clue.text: Crown painter seen around New England

clue.text: Talbot in a disorderly lot of soldiers

explanation.surface: A man called Talbot among an unruly bunch of soldiers.

clue.text: Narcotic report?

clue.text: Burns's sweet flower

clue.text: No room here for the Council Chamber!
